title: Websites Rush to Fix a Big Security Problem
summary:
On Wednesday, people around the world hurried to protect websites from a big security problem.

The problem was a weak spot in PHP. PHP is a computer language that millions of websites use. The FBI and the National Security Agency warned that hackers could use the weak spot to take control of websites. Hackers might also get private information.

To fix it, workers added security patches. A patch is a small update that closes a weak spot in software. While they worked, some government websites were turned off for a while. Some were still offline.

The company OpenAI says its artificial intelligence, or AI, helped find the problems.

This is why updates matter. When a weak spot is found, a fix is made, and people need to install it fast. You can help keep your own devices safe by keeping them up to date.
why_it_matters: Keeping your own devices updated helps protect your games, schoolwork and information from hackers.

keywords.explanation: Security means keeping something safe from harm or attack.
Hackers are people who break into computers without permission.
Patches are small updates that fix weak spots in software.
Software is the set of programs that tell a computer what to do.
Offline means not connected to the internet or not working online.
Artificial intelligence is computer technology that can do tasks that usually need human thinking.
